can_answer: partly: the file can compare the share of recorded crashes involving a death by clock time, but cannot establish exposure-adjusted risk
metric: annual percentage of eligible crashes with at least one person killed, by time of day
denominator: eligible crash rows with a nonmissing, non-midnight crash_time and nonmissing number_of_persons_killed (count of rows)
population: police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes in calendar years fully covered by the file, with non-ambiguous usable time and a complete person-killed total
filters: exclude calendar years not fully covered by the file
exclude rows with NULL or 00:00 crash_time because midnight may be default-coded
years: all fully covered calendar years in the file, determined from crash_date coverage in the data check

data_check.coverage: The file spans 2012-07-01 through 2026-06-11; 2012 (100,545 rows) and 2026 (36,424 rows) are partial calendar years and are excluded. Fully covered years are 2013–2025.
data_check.row_quality: In 2013–2025 crash_time is NULL on 0 rows and number_of_persons_killed is missing on 36 rows; 23,787 rows have a midnight time that may be default-coded, with possible overlap between missing-death and midnight rows.
data_check.decision: Exclude midnight-coded rows from night/day comparisons because the check finds a sharp increase from 24 in 2015 to 2,895 in 2016 and the field cannot establish whether these are true midnight times; exclude rows with missing death totals rather than imputing.
data_check.denominator_change: Eligible denominator rows decline from 208,341 in 2019 to 111,076 in 2020, a decrease of 97,265; changes in a crash-row denominator can affect the measured fatal-crash share, so compare these years with caution.

limitations: The data check excludes partial years 2012 and 2026, 23,787 midnight-coded rows that may be default-coded, and 36 rows missing person-killed totals (with overlap possible); no NULL times were found. The largest neighboring eligible-denominator change is a 97,265-row decrease from 2019 to 2020. Fatal-crash prevalence is not exposure-adjusted risk, and crash records contain no traffic-volume denominator.
